finding: Possible happy-path-only coverage of earliest_park_until: only one parked agent is ever tested, so the min-selection is never exercised.
why: team.py computes the earliest time with sorted(...)[0] over several parked agents (including ones with an empty park_until), but the fixture has a single parked agent, so a wrong pick (max, first-in-list) would still pass.
fix: Add a case with two or more parked agents (later one listed first, one with no park_until) and assert the earliest value.

finding: The new RENDER["team"] function, the feature-rounds chip, and the nav-dot/tooltip change have no behavioural test.
why: The only shell check is a substring grep for 'RENDER["team"]' and the NAV_KEYS length, so a JS error (such as a wrong field name or a missing d.* key) would pass every test and show 'failed to render' to the user.
fix: Add a test that runs the shell's render for a team VM and a progress VM, or at least asserts the data keys the JS reads exist in the VM.
evidence: test_registered_in_every_lockstep_table: `self.assertIn('RENDER["team"]', shell)`; JS reads d.feature, d.owning_session, d.owner_generation, d.states, d.counts, d.earliest_park_until, d.agents, d.processes

why: ADR-0015 and the contract promise only-adds with each existing caller's contract unchanged, yet an existing live section that answers Absent now gets a grey dot (was green) and a tooltip (was digest-only), with no test pinning it.

criterion: caller whose contract the diff changed, not updated
finding: GLOSSARY.md:273 still says live sections derive from the plan's artifacts, but the team section now reads the main checkout's .claude/afk-team manifest.
why: The INV-083 ledger lists GLOSSARY.md:273 as a site this change breaks; the slice leaves it stale (it sits outside the slice's Scope globs, so it needs a bounce or IOU, not a silent skip).
fix: Route a one-line GLOSSARY.md:273 update to its steward or record an anchored IOU.

finding: test_never_raises loops over three unrelated bad-manifest inputs in one test body.
why: The three failure kinds (invalid JSON, wrong format_version, recursion bomb) share one test, so a failure names only text[:20] and later inputs are skipped after the first failure.
fix: Use subTest or split into one test per bad input.

finding: Possible timing-dependent watch test: fixed sleeps plus a 5 s wall-clock poll over a watcher with its own poll interval.
why: The pass depends on the watcher's poll and debounce finishing inside 5 s and on the 0.3 s sleep; a slow CI host could flake it.
fix: Take the deadline from the server's _POLL_INTERVAL plus the debounce with generous headroom, or wait on a render/token signal instead of sleeping.
